Perfect Fit - It seems every refrigerator manual still recommends using copper tubing to hook up a water source. Don't go there. Each end has a fitting designed for a 1/4-inch compression joint and worked perfectly. You'll need a 1/2-inch wrench to tighten. The braided covering over the 1/4-inch tubing appears to be polyester or something similar; it doesn't restrict the movement of the tubing and is designed to protect it from abrasions and cuts. A few tips from my installation experience:

(1) Make sure yor drill a hole in your over-the-range cabinet about 1mm wider than 6 inches
(2) Make sure the 6 inch hole is located at the same distance from the back wall. The product does not come up with a paper template. It makes drilling the correct holes near impossible.
(3) This thing is HEAVY at around 35lb. You will need 2 people to do it right.
(4) The screws that come with the product are too short. I ended up using my own.
(5) The grills are very tight to be removed. Each grill fin is super sharp. Watch your fingers (I got 2 cuts)

The thing I hate:
(a) The cable length is a total joke ... why only 3 inches out (if from the top) or 1 inch out (if from the rear) if it does not come with a power plug? So, when you install, you need to be very precise in drilling a 2-3 inches hole in the cabinet that match the power wires.

Check your air vent gasket before ordering - Used this replacement gasket on a Kenmore 665.13402N411 dishwasher (2015). This is correct gasket to replace original on air vent W10469575. OEM gasket on vent was glued in. All videos I saw showed easy removal of old and fit of new. More of a project than I was expecting. I heated the gasket with a hair dryer and started pulling it out about 1/2" at a time. For more stubborn areas I dripped mineral spirits on the remaining gasket bits and let them sit for about 15-20 minutes then used an Xacto knife and a small plastic tool to remove the rest. Cleaned with soap and water dried 100% THEN fitted the new gasket. It stopped leaking by 99% and I think it is getting seated. However...

Check your leaking gasket to make sure it has easy removal. If not order part W10469575 if fan inside the door is still working. W10469574 if fan is kaput. Sears Parts Direct has the best videos I have found.

Gasket seems to be ok. Time will tell if it gets seated 100%. Shame on Whirlpool for using a rubber type glue to seat the OEM gasket.

UPDATE: we've run about (5) loads of dishes, pans, etc. through the dishwasher and the leak seems to have stopped completely. Rating now at (5) stars.

Has a HUGE Safety Issue-Potential Gas Leak - I bought this gas stove less than 5 mo. ago and have run into a very serious design flaw. And thought I have to tell folks about this.

You know how you have to push the knobs in & turn to ignite gas burners- well these knobs need VERY, very little depressing, and they turn very easily too, and a slight turn or bump releases gas without causing the auto ignitor to go on, plus they are high output burners- the combination makes for a GAS LEAK.
It has happened several times to both my partner & myself without noticing until we smell gas. Happens when we're cooking, sometimes happens we reach up to use the microwave above the stove, happened when our dog tried to stove surf-which really freaked us out.
Just yesterday a friend was over and began fixing a cup of coffee on the counter, next to the stove. I guess she may have grazed it with her body as she moved, within a few minutes we all began to smell gas, and we knew just where to check. Sure enough, the damn knob(s).
Some of the knobs seem to protrude out slightly further than the bar/oven handle-so the handle offers no protection of the knobs getting bumped.
Not sure if this problem is limited to our stove, but I would seriously check this stove out in person at a store first before purchasing.

I am not sure where/who to report this potentially deadly problem to, but thought I mention it here first where there is a significant amt of traffic.
